text:
alex: Hey team — seeing a weird spike in what I'm calling 'ghost' accounts. ~1.2k accounts with event_count = 0 but created in the last 5 days from imports. Healthscore pipeline returned -999 for a bunch and they're surfacing in renewal risk queues.
alex: Sample query I ran:
```sql
SELECT id, email, import_batch_id, created_at, event_count
FROM crm.accounts
WHERE event_count = 0 AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
LIMIT 50;
```
alex: Can we do a short-term mitigation: 1) exclude these from aggregate healthscore calc, 2) mark them with a tag (ghost:true) and route to an owner-nudge playbook instead of renewal emails, and 3) run a small backfill to set onboarding_status='imported' for the batch? Thoughts?
cs-ops-bot: alert: healthscore.anomaly detected — 1,238 accounts matching (event_count=0, created_at within 7d). Auto-notified #customer-success. :rotating_light:
marta: do we know which import job(s) created these? import_batch_id shows some values or is it null in the sample?
kevin: in my quick look most have import_batch_id not null. quick mitigation: add pre-filter in healthscore service to ignore accounts where event_count = 0 AND import_batch_id IS NOT NULL AND created_at > (now() - interval '14 days')
kevin: also recommend tagging so downstream reports know they're import-no-activity. sample playbook patch (curl example):
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.local/api/playbooks/rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "suppress-ghost-imports",
    "match": "event_count = 0 AND import_batch_id IS NOT NULL AND created_at > now() - interval '14 days'",
    "action": "tag:ghost, route:owner_nudge, suppress_healthscore: true"
  }'
```
jamie: I can run the backfill to set onboarding_status='imported' and add tag ghost:true for those import_batch_ids. I'll scope to import_batch_id IN (...) rather than blanket.
jamie: running backfill job as `backfill-ghosts-1745` now, ETA ~25-45m. Will post the job id and sample rows after run.
alex: thanks. can we also suppress the renewal-alerts pipeline for these accounts for 48h so customers don't get churn nudges while we investigate? put a 48h snooze and a runbook note.
kevin: i'll open a tiny PR for the playbook config change and add the filter to the healthscore preprocessor. @marta can you review once it's up?
marta: on it, will review in next 20.
cs-ops-bot: playbook.deploy triggered by kevin (pr/4827). status: queued.
alex: perfect. jamie — ping me when the backfill job id is up so I can attach to the runbook: https://redwood.company/runbooks/cs/ghost-accounts
jamie: backfill job complete: id backfill-ghosts-1745, touched 1,212 accounts. sample updated row: `id=acct_9f3a, onboarding_status=imported, tags=["ghost"]`
cs-ops-bot: alert: healthscore.anomaly resolved — 1,212 accounts moved to onboarding_status=imported and tagged. playbook.suppress-ghost-imports deployed. :white_check_mark:
alex: awesome — follow-ups: (1) kevin please merge and deploy the pre-filter rule, (2) marta update the runbook with root-cause notes and the import_batch ids, (3) i'll monitor renewal queue for 24h. thanks all. :tada:
